INL error is the maximum deviation between an actual code transition point and its corresponding ideal transition point (straight line). Figure 2-5 shows the INL curve of the MCP4725. The end-point method is used for the calculation. The INL error at a given input DAC code is calculated as:
I N L = \frac {\left(V _ {O U T} - V _ {I d e a l}\right)}{L S B}
\begin{array}{r c l} \mathrm{V} _ {\text {Ideal}} & = & \text {Code*LSB} \\ \mathrm{V} _ {\text {OUT}} & = & \text {The output voltage measured at} \\ & & \text {the given input code} \end{array}

Differential nonlinearity error (Figure 4-2) is the measure of step size between codes in actual transfer function. The ideal step size between codes is 1 LSB. A DNL error of zero would imply that every code is exactly 1 LSB wide. If the DNL error is less than 1 LSB, the DAC guarantees monotonic output and no missing codes. The DNL error between any two adjacent codes is calculated as follows:
D N L = \frac {\Delta V _ {O U T} - L S B}{L S B}
\begin{array}{r l r} \Delta V _ {\text {OUT}} & = & \text {The measured DAC output} \\ & & \text {voltage difference between two} \\ & & \text {adjacent input codes.} \end{array}

For the output capacitor, it is recommended to use of small ceramic capacitors placed as close as possible to the VOUT and PGND pins of the IC. The recommended nominal output capacitors are three times 22 µF. If, for any reason, the application requires the use of large capacitors that cannot be placed close to the IC, use a smaller ceramic capacitor in parallel to the large capacitor. Place the small capacitor as close as possible to the VOUT and PGND pins of the IC.

There are no additional requirements regarding minimum ESR. There is also no upper limit for the output capacitance value. Larger capacitors cause lower output voltage ripple as well as lower output voltage drop during load transients.

A 10 µF input capacitor is recommended to improve line transient behavior of the regulator and EMI behavior of the total power supply circuit. An X5R or X7R ceramic capacitor placed as close as possible to the VIN and PGND pins of the IC is recommended. This capacitance can be increased without limit. If the input supply is located more than a few inches from the TPS6302x converter, additional bulk capacitance can be required in addition to the ceramic bypass capacitors. An electrolytic or tantalum capacitor with a value of $4 7 ~ \mu \mathsf { F }$ is a typical choice.

To make sure that the internal control circuits are supplied with a stable low noise supply voltage, a capacitor can be connected between VINA and GND. Using a ceramic capacitor with a value of 0.1 µF is recommended. The value of this capacitor must not be higher than 0.22 µF.

When the adjustable output voltage version TPS63020 is used, the output voltage is set by an external resistor divider. The resistor divider must be connected between VOUT, FB, and GND. The feedback voltage is 500 mV nominal. The low-side resistor R2 (between FB and GND) must be kept in the range of 200 kΩ. Use Equation 3 to calculate the high-side resistor R1 (between VOUT and FB).

There are no additional requirements regarding minimum ESR. There is also no upper limit for the output capacitance value. Larger capacitors cause lower output voltage ripple as well as lower output voltage drop during load transients.
